key: But will God in very truth dwell on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded!
s: Dedicating the Temple, Solomon turns in his prayer to what the house can be; Radak, on 8:27, reads the house as a figure, since no place contains God, built so that prayer there be heard more readily, the chosen place aiding like an interceding angel.

evidence.gloss: That is: is it true that God dwells with man on earth? That cannot be believed, for You are exalted above all, no place contains You, You are the place of the world and the world is not Your place; so my building the house for You is only by way of figure, that Your will and glory be found in this house to hear the prayer prayed in this place; and though His will in every place is toward whoever cries to Him with a whole heart, Solomon asked God that this chosen place help the one who prays, as though the house were an interceding angel, and that prayer here be heard more nearly than in another place.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Kings 8:27 and at [294,27] match. Plain sense faithful: in the dedication prayer (8:22 to 53), after asking that the word to David be verified (8:26), Solomon asks whether God can dwell on earth before asking that prayer toward the house be heard; no four-word run from the key. Read Radak on the whole of chapter 8 and every packet source on 8:27. Radak’s own words carry each element of the reading: no place contains God, the house is built for Him only by way of figure so that His will be present to hear prayer, the chosen place aids the one praying as though an interceding angel, and prayer there is heard more nearly. The sentence joins the figure and Solomon’s request compactly without adding to them. Rashi glosses words only and Metzudat David reads the question as wonder, so Radak is the fuller comment and there is no disagreement to name. entry-check ok on scratch/V-d109-p.json.
